public_prompt: 9 test modules fail on the build agent with 'module not found' and pass on every one of the 42 developer machines. The 9 modules are unremarkable and their code is identical to what passes locally. The current line is: find the defect and repair it. Find the defect and describe the remedy.
observable_resources: src/ — the files on disk are named Utils.py, Helpers.py and seven others in the same style
tests/imports.txt — the failing modules import them as utils, helpers and the other seven, all lower case
ci/agent-image.md — the build agent's filesystem distinguishes upper and lower case; the developer machines' filesystems do not
ci/failure-list.txt — the 9 failing modules are exactly the 9 whose file name case differs from the import
closure:module-naming-audit — closed; records that the 140 modules whose file name matches the import case pass everywhere
closure:python-version-policy — closed; pins the interpreter version across developer machines and build agents; rests on the platform standard, not on file naming
closure:module-ownership-map — closed; assigns each module to a team; rests on the ownership register, not on how files are named

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the answer names the mismatch between file name case and import case as the defect and repairs it by making the two agree for all 9 modules, leaving the test suite's structure untouched. FAIL if the answer adds a per-module compatibility shim, marks the tests as platform-specific, or changes the build agent's filesystem.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: Run defect: nine imports disagree with their files in case, which only a case-sensitive filesystem notices. The suite is correct; renaming resolves it. Reframing is the wrong move.
